title: Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Adam at the right hand of power — the trial, Psalm 110 and Daniel 7 at his own mouth (Mark 14; Acts 7; Hebrews 1)
summary:
It ain't new. The high priest puts him under oath, and the answer is two scriptures:

*Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Matthew 26:64)

Mark hears the plain word before the scriptures:

*And Yahusha (Jesus) said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Mark 14:62)

The seat is David's psalm:

*Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* (Psalm 110:1)

He had already set that psalm before the Pharisees in the temple and asked them a question nobody answered:

*If David then call him Adonai (Lord), how is he his son?* (Matthew 22:45)

The clouds are Daniel's:

*I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13)

*And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14)

Daniel says *like* the Son of Adam, because he was shown a figure who looked like a man and was more than one. At the trial the man standing in the room says it of himself without the *like*: the one Daniel saw is the one under oath, and the everlasting dominion of the next verse is his. Daniel keeps his *like*; the trial is where the name is claimed outright. The high priest understood both scriptures and what they say together:

*Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.* (Matthew 26:65)

He tore his clothes because the one at the right hand of Yahuah (the LORD), the one who comes with the clouds, had just said he was the man in front of him. He is Elohim (God) and he has a Father: the psalm has two speakers, the vision has the Ancient of days and the one brought before him, and the trial has the same two.

The seat was taken soon after. Stephen saw it, and the letters keep returning to it:

*But he, being full of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of Elohim (God), and Yahusha (Jesus) standing on the right hand of Elohim (God),* (Acts 7:55)

*Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* (Hebrews 1:3)

And the coming with the clouds is still ahead, said in his own words on the mount and in John's words at the opening of the Revelation, each book speaking for itself:

*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30)

*Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.* (Revelation 1:7)

Two scriptures, said under oath, condemned him to death. They are the two the whole library goes on saying of him.

3010.prose: Before the oath, Yahusha (Jesus) had already put a question himself. In the temple he asked the Pharisees whose son the Messiah (Christ) is, and led them into David's psalm. At the trial he answers it from the seat itself: *sitting on the right hand of power*.
3010.phrase: While the Pharisees were gathered together
3010.sentence: The question put to the Pharisees opens the psalm that Yahusha (Jesus) later answers at the trial.

3012.prose: Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* come *with the clouds of heaven* and be brought to the Ancient of days. Yahusha (Jesus) says *coming in the clouds of heaven* of himself, and drops the *like*. Daniel keeps his word. The man under oath claims the name outright.
3012.phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven
3012.sentence: Daniel's figure is one like the Son of Adam, shown coming with the clouds to the Ancient of days.

3014.prose: Luke gives the same answer in fewer words. *Hereafter* opens it again, and the seat is *the right hand of the power*. The very next verse shows the room hearing it as a claim to be the Son of Elohim (God), and Yahusha (Jesus) does not take it back.
3014.phrase: Hereafter shall the Son of Adam sit on the right hand of the power
3014.sentence: Luke records the same answer about the seat, and the room takes it as a claim to be the Son of Elohim (God).

3015.prose: At the trial the seat was still ahead: *Hereafter shall ye see*. Stephen looks up and sees Yahusha (Jesus) *standing on the right hand of Elohim (God)*. The seat named under oath is seen taken, and in the next verse Stephen himself calls him the Son of Adam.
3015.phrase: and Yahusha (Jesus) standing on the right hand of Elohim (God)
3015.sentence: Stephen sees Yahusha (Jesus) at the right hand of Elohim (God), the seat named at the trial.

3016.prose: Peter points out that David did not go up to heaven, so *Sit thou on my right hand* is not said of David. It is said to another. The psalm has two speakers, *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord*, and Yahusha (Jesus) is the one who sits where the psalm sets him.
3016.phrase: he saith himself, Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand
3016.sentence: The psalm David spoke is the same one Yahusha (Jesus) answered with at the trial, now read as said to him.

3017.prose: Paul asks who can condemn. The high priest and the council had condemned Yahusha (Jesus) to death. Paul's answer is that the one who died is *risen again* and *at the right hand of Elohim (God)*, the seat he told them they would see.
3017.phrase: that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of Elohim (God)
3017.sentence: The one condemned to death is risen and sits at the right hand of Elohim (God), as he said at the trial.

3018.prose: The man condemned at the trial is raised and set in the seat he said they would see. Paul says Elohim (God) *raised him from the dead* and put him at *his own right hand*. The council's verdict ended in death, and the seat came after it.
3018.phrase: when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand
3018.sentence: Raised from the dead, he is set at the right hand, the place named at the trial.

3019.prose: Paul points to where Messiah (Christ) *sitteth on the right hand of Elohim (God)*. That is the seat Yahusha (Jesus) told the council about. What was a warning to the high priest is now the place Paul says to look toward.
3019.phrase: where Messiah (Christ) sitteth on the right hand of Elohim (God)
3019.sentence: Messiah (Christ) is seated at the right hand of Elohim (God), the seat spoken of at the trial.

3020.prose: *Right hand of power* at the trial becomes *the right hand of the Majesty on high* here. It is the same seat under another name. The letter says he sat down after he *purged our sins*, so the seat is taken after the work is done, by the Son who is *the express image of his person*.
3020.phrase: sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high
3020.sentence: The seat Yahusha (Jesus) named under oath is described here as the right hand of the Majesty on high.

3021.prose: The letter asks which angel was ever told *Sit on my right hand*, and the answer is none. The words belong to the Son. They come from the psalm Yahusha (Jesus) set before the Pharisees and then answered with at the trial, when he said he would sit at the right hand of power.
3021.phrase: Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool
3021.sentence: Only the Son was ever told to sit at the right hand, which is the seat he claimed at the trial.

3024.prose: He *endured the cross, despising the shame*, and the end of it is the seat. The man who stood bound before the council is set down *at the right hand of the throne*, as he told them they would see.
3024.phrase: and is set down at the right hand of the throne of Elohim (God)
3024.sentence: After the cross he is set down at the right hand, the seat named before the council.

3027.prose: He spoke of the coming in the clouds on the mount before he spoke of it under oath. There the tribes of the earth see the Son of Adam coming *with power and great glory*. At the trial he tells the council the same sight is theirs to see. The same words, said twice.
3027.phrase: they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory
3027.sentence: The coming in the clouds is spoken first to his own and then to the high priest, still ahead in both.

3028.prose: The trial says sitting and coming. This verse puts both in one sentence: the Son of Adam *shall come in his glory*, and then *sit upon the throne of his glory*. The right hand of power that the high priest heard about is shown here as a throne.
3028.phrase: When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him
3028.sentence: The Son of Adam comes in glory and sits on a throne, joining the coming and the sitting he named at the trial.

6992.prose: At the bed of the man with palsy, Yahusha (Jesus) already speaks of himself as the Son of Adam, who *hath power on earth to forgive sins*. Long before the trial he used that name for himself. The council later hears it again with the seat and the clouds attached.
6992.phrase: But that ye may know that the Son of Adam hath power on earth to forgive sins
6992.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) called himself the Son of Adam well before the trial, where the same name carries the seat and the clouds.

5157.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam *cometh in the glory of his Father*. Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* brought near *before him*, the Ancient of days. There are two in the vision, one who comes and one he comes to, and the Son of Adam has a Father. Daniel's *like* stays Daniel's.
5157.phrase: came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him
5157.sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days, one who comes and one he comes to.

7116.prose: Luke gives only the seat. The psalm gives the voice that sets it: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord*. One speaks and one sits. Yahusha (Jesus) says he is the one who will sit there, until *thine enemies* become a *footstool*.
7116.phrase: Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool
7116.sentence: The psalm's seat is the one Yahusha (Jesus) says he will take, set by one who speaks to another.

5159.prose: He warned that the Son of Adam would come in glory, and here he says it to the men about to condemn him. He does not hide it. *Thou hast said*, he tells the high priest, and then names the seat and the clouds.
5159.phrase: Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power
5159.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says to the high priest what he had already said to his own, the Son of Adam seated and coming.

5158.prose: On the road he spoke of the Son of Adam in the third person. Before the high priest he says *I am*, and the seat and the clouds follow in the same breath. The title he used of himself is now claimed plainly, under oath, in front of those who could condemn him.
5158.phrase: I am: and ye shall see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power
5158.sentence: At the trial he answers I am, and names the Son of Adam as himself.

5325.prose: They led Yahusha (Jesus) to the high priest, with the chief priests, elders and scribes gathered. The psalm is the answer waiting in that room: *Sit thou at my right hand*, with *thine enemies* made a *footstool*. In that room the psalm's seat is named aloud.
5325.phrase: Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool
5325.sentence: The psalm's seat is the answer Yahusha (Jesus) gives once the council is assembled.

5326.prose: The whole court is gathered, and the high priest's question puts Daniel's vision in the room. Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* and *they brought him near* the Ancient of days. The man standing before the court says the figure is himself, and he says it without the *like*.
5326.phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven
5326.sentence: Daniel's vision of one like the Son of Adam is what the gathered council hears claimed of the man before them.

5388.prose: At the trial he said *ye shall see* the Son of Adam *sitting on the right hand of power*. Mark ends with him received up, and he *sat on the right hand of Elohim (God)*. The seat is no longer only promised. The book that records the promise records the taking.
5388.phrase: I am: and ye shall see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power
5388.sentence: What was said at the trial about the seat is told in Mark as done.

5390.prose: Mark says he sat on the right hand of Elohim (God). Stephen sees it for himself, and looks up to see Yahusha (Jesus) *standing on the right hand of Elohim (God)*. One says sat and the other says standing, and the place is the same: at the right hand.
5390.phrase: and Yahusha (Jesus) standing on the right hand of Elohim (God)
5390.sentence: Stephen sees Yahusha (Jesus) at the right hand, where Mark says he sat.

5391.prose: Mark says he *sat on the right hand of Elohim (God)*. Hebrews says it again in other words: he *sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high*, when *he had by himself purged our sins*. The same seat is told twice, once as an act and once as a name.
5391.phrase: when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high
5391.sentence: Hebrews names the seat Mark describes as the right hand of the Majesty on high.
